narrative.overview:
The organizer is drawn as São Paulo Metrô wayfinding. A black sign bar carries white grotesque type; categories are metro lines, shown as numbered color discs; the week is a line with seven stations, each a ringed stop on a heavy black rail. The month is a hairline mesh on concrete-grey ground, so the page reads like a printed network map, not like a stack of app cards.

Density is high and calm. Hierarchy comes from weight (one grotesque from 400 to 800) and from the rail, not from boxes, shadows or color fills. Color is information: line colors identify category, yellow says "here, now, this one", red marks Sundays, holidays, errors and delete. Everything else is ink on concrete. The world refuses the category default for organizers: white rounded cards, a grey sidebar and a single blue accent.

The system runs in light and dark schemes. Dark keeps the same signage logic: the sign bar goes pure black, neutrals invert, and yellow moves from a fill to a pair of 2px rules so the band stays legible on dark ground.
keyCharacteristics: Black sign bar (72px, 56px on phones) with white grotesque type and a 4px yellow underline on the active tab.
Categories as numbered SP Metrô line discs; never as colored boxes.
The week as a station rail: 6px rail, 26px stops with a 6px ring, today filled yellow.
1px hairline mesh with 2px strong rules as section heads; zero radius on every rectangle.
One typeface (Archivo), tabular numerals for every time, date and count.
Done is a state, not a deletion: struck through, or stamped green with its date.

rules.name: The Signal Yellow Rule
rules.body: Yellow means "here, now, this one": active tab, today, selected station, drop target, hover on the primary action. It never decorates chrome, never fills a button at rest, and its only categorical use is the line 4 disc.

rules.name: The Line Is a Disc Rule
rules.body: A category color appears only as a numbered disc or a 10px chip dot. It never tints a card, cell, border or text.

rules.name: The Red Calendar Rule
rules.body: Red text belongs to the calendar (Sundays, holidays) and to danger (delete, invalid). Line 3 is a disc, never red text.

rules.name: The One Grotesque Rule
rules.body: Archivo is the only face. Hierarchy is made with weight and size, never a second family.

rules.name: The Tabular Clock Rule
rules.body: Every time, day number, date, count and disc numeral is set with tabular figures so columns align like a departure board.

rules.name: The Flat Platform Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the grid casts a shadow at rest. Lift is for things in transit (dragging) or announcements floating above the map (toast).

rules.name: The Mesh and Stop Rule
rules.body: Rectangles are 0px, circles are 50%. There is no third shape and no in-between radius.

dos: Do show a category as its numbered line disc (or a 10px dot in tight calendar cells), using the `App.LINES` value and its matching numeral color.
Do keep yellow for "here and now": active tab, today, the selected station, drop targets, and the primary hover underline.
Do draw structure with rules: 1px hairline mesh, 2px ink section rules, the 6px rail.
Do set every time, date, number and count in Archivo with tabular figures.
Do show done as a state (struck through in Tertiary Ink, or the green stamp with its date); finished things stay visible until the user clears them.
Do carry both schemes through the custom properties: in dark, the band becomes yellow rules on warm black, not a yellow fill.
Do keep touch targets at 40px or more under coarse pointers.
donts: Don't round a rectangle. Cells, buttons, inputs and cards stay at 0px; only stops, discs, marks and dots are circles.
Don't fill a card, cell or border with a category color, and don't set text in a line color.
Don't use yellow as decoration, as a resting button fill, or for anything that isn't the current or targeted thing.
Don't introduce a second typeface or proportional numerals in a time column.
Don't add ambient shadows to resting surfaces; Lift is only for the drag ghost and the toast.
Don't fall back to the organizer default: white rounded cards, a grey sidebar, one blue accent.
